tools.name: ask_human_developer
tools.title: Ask a human developer
tools.description: Saves a draft request to a real, manually approved human developer: a question, a code review, a consultation or hands-on help with a software problem. It takes a short summary in plain words, which must not contain passwords, API keys, tokens or other secrets. Only a draft is saved: nothing reaches a developer until it is sent, and nothing is charged. It returns the exact saved text and a task_id.

summary.description: What the person needs, in plain words: what is wrong or what they want help with, what they were doing, and what has already been tried. No secrets.

tool.description: The AI tool the app was built with, if known.

availability.description: When the person is free for a call, for example 'weekdays after 5pm CET'. Optional.

tools.name: send_request
tools.title: Send a request to developers
tools.description: Sends a saved draft to approved developers. It works only for a draft this connection saved in the last 30 minutes, and each person can send only a few per day. The person receives an email copy with a link to cancel. Nothing is charged. The optional text is compared with the saved draft, and nothing is sent if it differs.

task_id.description: The draft to send: the task_id that ask_human_developer returned.

text.description: The exact saved text, to confirm what is being sent. If it differs from the saved draft, nothing is sent.

tools.name: get_task_status
tools.title: See where a request stands
tools.description: Returns where the user's requests stand: a fixed state, a next_action (send_request, respond_to_call_time, person_decides_on_website, join_call, wait or none), the call time in the user's own time zone and a link to the request page. With no task_id it lists the most recent requests. Read-only. It never returns text written by a developer. Prices, approvals and cards are never handled by this connector.

task_id.description: The request to look at. Leave it out to list the most recent ones.

tools.name: respond_to_call_time
tools.title: Answer a call time
tools.description: Answers a call time for a request. 'accept' confirms the time a developer proposed, or the new time a developer asked for. 'decline' says it does not work: before the call is booked another developer is asked, afterwards the booked time stays. 'propose_other_time' suggests a new time for a booked call; the developer is emailed and answers. Times are shown in the user's own time zone; new times are ISO 8601 with an offset.

task_id.description: The request the call is for.

time.description: Only for propose_other_time: the new start as ISO 8601 with an offset, for example 2026-11-12T15:00:00+01:00.
